summary: Unexpected cross-region fallthrough when customer pins region causing 60-120ms latency delta
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after enabling a region pin for their dedicated capacity (pin_region=us-east), ~1-2% of requests are observed routing to eu-west and returning with a 60-120ms higher p50. This started after a traffic shift last week. Impact: user-facing inference latency spikes for a subset of requests; intermittent degradation for real-time product features.
impact: Intermittent +60-120ms p50 for ~1-2% of inference requests. Affects time-sensitive features and violates internal latency targets for FinLedger workflows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer app makes streaming chat completions to Redwood endpoint pinned to us-east (pin_region=us-east). 2) Observe per-request region header in response metadata. 3) Compare p50/p95 from customer telemetry and Redwood tracing for same request IDs. 4) Repeat during higher load to increase probability of fallthrough.
observed_behavior: Some requests (sampled) show response_metadata.region = eu-west and corresponding latency delta. Requests include 'x-rw-request-id' headers and appear to have been handled by fallback routing logic.
expected_behavior: When pin_region is set to an explicit region and customer has Dedicated capacity in that region, all requests should remain in the pinned region unless an explicit outage/fallback policy triggers, and fallbacks should be documented and deterministic.
request_examples_and_traces: Example request-id: rw-req-20260311-4823. Timestamp: 2026-03-11T14:22:07Z. Customer trace shows 96ms total, Redwood trace shows 174ms and 'route_decision': 'fallback-eu-west' in internal routing log. Another request rw-req-20260312-0192 shows similar pattern.
attached_logs: Attached: routing-decision.log (excerpt), request-trace-20260311.txt. Routing log lines: [2026-03-11T14:22:07Z] rw-req-4823 route_decision=FALLBACK target_region=eu-west reason=pool_capacity_low pinned_region=us-east; [2026-03-11T14:22:08Z] rw-req-0192 route_decision=FALLBACK target_region=eu-west reason=allocator_threshold_exceeded pinned_region=us-east.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: fallback policy is allowed for dedicated customers when local pool capacity falls below allocator_threshold. We confirmed via routing logs that the decision path labels these as FALLBACK and target eu-west. Checked Dedicated capacity metrics in the last 24h: short spikes in queue_length on us-east GPU pool during customer peak. Batching and placement attempts were observed to spill over. No errors or 5xx returned. Observed correlation between queue pressure events and fallthrough samples.
support_thread_summary: Customer provided timeseries and sample request IDs. Support reproduced trace correlation with our routing logs. SRE asked for full allocator metrics and pool sizes. Product asked whether 'pin_region' semantics should be 'strict' vs 'best-effort' for Dedicated customers; current behavior is best-effort with documented fallbacks but customer expected strict locality.
comments: 2026-03-11 15:02 - FinLedger (customer): We're seeing a small fraction of requests go to eu-west despite pin_region=us-east. This is causing brief UI hitches. Can you explain why?
2026-03-11 16:10 - Aisha Khan (Support): Thanks — we've captured request IDs. Investigating routing decisions and pool pressure. Can you confirm if you had any capacity scaling changes last 24h?
2026-03-11 17:05 - FinLedger: No manual changes. Traffic increased ~20% due to a marketing campaign.

2026-03-12 09:30 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Found 'FALLBACK' decisions in routing logs tied to allocator_threshold_exceeded. Short-term queue spikes caused placement to select eu-west where capacity available. No errors observed; falls back based on configured policy.
2026-03-12 11:45 - Product (Lina Patel): We should clarify region pinning semantics in documentation and consider exposing a strict_pin option for Dedicated tiers. Logged product follow-up.
2026-03-13 08:20 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Provided workaround to customer: increase reserved capacity in us-east or set fallback_policy=no_fallback (note: may result in increased 429s if pool saturated).
proposed_workarounds: 1) Increase reserved capacity for FinLedger's Dedicated pool in us-east to reduce spillover. 2) Temporarily set fallback_policy=no_fallback in customer's routing config to enforce strict locality (tradeoff: higher chance of 429s under load). 3) Tune allocator_threshold to be more conservative for this customer's pools.
resolution_notes: Short-term: Customer agreed to increase reserved capacity by 20% and set fallback_policy=no_fallback for the critical route. After change, sampling over 24h shows fallthrough events dropped to 0. Long-term: Product will add explicit 'strict_pin' flag for Dedicated customers to make behavior deterministic and surface consequences in Console and API docs. SRE created INT-3419 to track allocator tuning and autoscaling policy improvements.
follow_up_actions: Create product feature request: strict_pin API option
Update docs: region pinning behavior and fallback policy tradeoffs
SRE to add allocator alerting for queue spikes on Dedicated pools
resolution_status: Workaround applied; monitoring indicates resolved for customer. Product feature queued.
